summary: Defines extensions to the pseudowire control protocol and its IANA allocations needed to set up time-division multiplexing (TDM) pseudowires over MPLS networks. TDM pseudowires carry traditional circuit-style telephone-type traffic across a packet network, and this document adds the signaling pieces they require. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: Old phone lines send a steady stream of timed pulses. This explains how to carry that stream through a modern packet network, like running an old train line through a new tunnel.

questions: how are tdm pseudowires set up with ldp
what is the tdm options interface parameter
subtitle: The LDP extensions that let two routers agree on how to carry a T1, E1 or similar circuit across an MPLS network.

tldr.problem: Time-division multiplexing (TDM) circuits such as E1 and T1 lines can be emulated over packet networks, but the two edge routers need to agree on the details before the emulated circuit can start.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines how to use the existing LDP pseudowire setup messages for TDM: which pseudowire types to use, seven interface parameters (one of them new in this RFC), and the status codes that report a mismatch.
tldr.outcome: Two ends can set up TDM pseudowires over MPLS in an interoperable way, and a failure to agree is reported with a defined status code.

today: RFC 5287 is a Proposed Standard from August 2008. The unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
RFC 5287 extends the pseudowire (PW) control protocol of RFC 4447 and the IANA allocations of RFC 4446 so that Time-Division Multiplexing (TDM) pseudowires can be set up in MPLS networks. The data formats themselves come from other documents: structure-agnostic TDM pseudowires are in RFC 4553, and structure-aware ones are in RFC 5086 and RFC 5087.

RFC 4447 uses the Label Distribution Protocol (LDP) to exchange PW labels for services such as Ethernet, Frame Relay, ATM and HDLC. Setting up TDM pseudowires needs both a particular reading of the existing information elements and some additional information. Setup using L2TPv3 is left to a separate document.
sections.eli5: Old telephone-style lines can be carried over a modern network if both ends agree on the rules first. This document writes those rules down.

sections.title: The PW FEC and PW Types
sections.content:
LDP advertises the binding between a pseudowire and its label with a Label Mapping message. RFC 4447 defines two kinds of PW Forwarding Equivalence Class (FEC). The PWId FEC (FEC 128) holds the PW type, a control bit, a Group ID, a PW ID and an interface parameters sub-TLV. The Generalized PW FEC (FEC 129) holds the PW type, the control bit and an Attachment Group Identifier plus source and target attachment identifiers that replace the PW ID. Either one MAY be used for TDM PWs.

The TDM PW types come from RFC 4446, and the two endpoints MUST agree on the type because both directions of the PW have to be the same type. The control bit MUST always be set for TDM PWs, because all TDM encapsulations use a control word. Setting it to zero MUST result in the LDP status Illegal C-Bit. Type 0x0012 MUST also be used for structure-agnostic PWs between a pair of J1 attachment circuits.
sections.eli5: Before sending, both sides must name the kind of line they are carrying and agree on it. If they name different kinds, the connection is refused.

sections.title: Interface Parameters for TDM PWs
sections.content:
The interface parameters sub-TLVs carry the details of a TDM service. Values are unsigned integers of 16 or 32 bits unless stated otherwise. The RFC lists seven parameters: CEP/TDM Payload Bytes (0x04), CEP/TDM Bit-Rate (0x07), Number of TDMoIP AAL1 Cells per Packet (0x0E), TDMoIP AAL1 Mode (0x10), TDMoIP AAL2 Options (0x11), Fragmentation Indicator (0x09) and TDM Options (0x0B).

  • Payload Bytes is used for all SAToP and CESoPSN PWs. Both ends MUST agree on it, and it is OPTIONAL, with the service default assumed when omitted. For CESoPSN the value P MUST be an integer multiple of N, the number of timeslots. It MUST NOT be used for TDMoIP PWs.
  • Bit-Rate is given in multiples of 64 Kbit/s. For structure-agnostic emulation the values are 32 for E1, 24 for basic T1, 25 for octet-aligned T1, 535 for E3 and 699 for T3. For structure-aware emulation it MUST be N, the number of DS0 channels. The RFC notes that 24 is a convenience value and not the actual T1 rate.
  • AAL1 cells per packet MAY be present for TDMoIP AAL1 PWs and counts 48-byte AAL1 PDUs. It defaults to 1 for low bit-rates (32 or less) and 5 for 535 or 699.
  • AAL1 mode MAY be present: 0 is unstructured, 2 is structured and 3 is structured with CAS. It defaults to structured, and both ends MUST agree.
  • AAL2 options MUST be present for TDMoIP AAL2 PWs. It holds voice activity detection (V), an encoding, a Maximum Duration in units of 125 microseconds that MUST be less than 64 for unencoded 64 kbps channels, and optional CID mapping bases.
  • Fragmentation Indicator MUST be omitted for all TDM PWs except trunk-specific NxDS0 services with CAS using CESoPSN, where it MUST be present if the payload size P differs from N times the frames per trunk multiframe.
sections.eli5: These are the questions on the form: how big are the parcels, how fast is the line, and which wrapping style is used. Each has a number code so both sides read it the same way.

sections.title: The TDM Options Parameter
sections.content:
TDM Options is the one genuinely new parameter, with ID 0x0B assigned by IANA. Its length is 4, 8 or 12 bytes. It carries the following flags and fields.

  • R: the sender expects an RTP header in the encapsulation. RTP is used only if both ends expect it, and usage MUST match in both directions. When R is cleared, Length MUST be 4; otherwise it MUST be 8 or 12.
  • D: the sender expects the peer to use differential timestamping. This may be used in just one direction.
  • F and X: reserved, cleared on send and ignored on receipt.
  • SP: signaling packet support for CESoPSN. 00 means no signaling packets, 01 is a data PW expecting signaling in a separate PW, 10 is the PW carrying the signaling packets, and 11 is data and signaling on the same PW.
  • CAS: cleared except for trunk-specific NxDS0 services with CAS, where 01 is an E1 trunk, 10 is a T1/ESF trunk and 11 is a T1 SF trunk.
  • PT, FREQ and SSRC: the expected RTP payload type, the timestamping clock frequency in units of 8 kHz, and the expected RTP SSRC. A value of 0 for PT or SSRC means that check is not used.

The parameter MAY be omitted for plain SAToP without RTP, basic CESoPSN NxDS0 without CE signaling, TDMoIP AAL1 mode 0 or 2 without RTP, and TDMoIP AAL2 without CAS relay or RTP. It MUST be present for any PW that uses RTP, for CESoPSN PWs that use signaling packets, for trunk-specific NxDS0 with CAS, for TDMoIP AAL1 mode 1, and for AAL2 PWs that relay CAS.
sections.eli5: This is a small extra card with switches on it, such as whether to stamp every parcel with a clock reading. If a switch is turned on, it must be filled in and the other side must be able to do it too.

sections.title: Pairing Data and Signaling PWs
sections.content:
A basic CESoPSN NxDS0 service can carry CE application signaling, such as CAS, in special signaling packets sent over a separate PW. Section 4 sets the rules for matching such a pair. Both PWs MUST have the same PW type, use the same setup method (both PWId FEC or both Generalized PW FEC) and carry identical values for all the interface parameters, except for the SP bits. The data PW sets SP to 01 and the signaling PW sets it to 10.

With the PWId FEC, the data PW MUST have an even PW ID and the signaling PW MUST use the next (odd) value. With the Generalized PW FEC no matching rules are defined, and implementation-specific mechanisms MAY be used. If one of the pair fails to come up, or fails later, the other MUST be torn down.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the voice goes in one box and the control beeps go in a twin box. The twins must match, and if one is lost the other is thrown away too.

sections.title: LDP Status Codes and PW Status
sections.content:
Besides the codes in RFC 4447, the status codes of RFC 4446 MUST be used to explain why a TDM PW failed to come up. Incompatible bit-rate covers a mismatch of T1 encapsulation modes (basic against octet-aligned) or of the timeslot count. CEP/TDM misconfiguration covers mismatches in RTP header use, timestamping clock frequency, signaling packet behavior, AAL1 mode, and trunk framing for NxDS0 with CAS. The generic misconfiguration error MAY be used for any other failure.

After most misconfigurations the user MAY reconfigure the endpoints and try again, but a trunk framing mismatch in CAS services is fatal.

The TDM control word already carries attachment circuit and PSN status. The PW Status TLV can do similar work, but while the interworking function (IWF) is working its use is NOT RECOMMENDED, to avoid conflict between data-plane and control-plane indications. If the IWF itself fails while the control plane stays up, a Status TLV with all five fault bits set SHOULD be sent.
sections.eli5: When the two sides disagree, the router sends back a note that says which part did not match. Status flags are only used if the main machine breaks.

sections.title: IANA and Security
sections.content:
Most of the IANA assignments are already in RFC 4446. Four interface parameter sub-TLV types were added for this document: TDM Options (0x0B), Number of TDMoIP AAL1 cells per packet (0x0E), TDMoIP AAL1 mode (0x10) and TDMoIP AAL2 Options (0x11).

On security, the RFC says it has no additional impact beyond that of the basic LDP-based PW setup in RFC 4447.
sections.eli5: The code numbers were reserved in the official list, and this adds no new safety worries.
